# `set_sequence`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Create or patch imaging sequence entries, by id.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (full command-socket call; shared diagnostic writes; 64-bit and 32-bit builds) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xd0500 (64-bit build) |

params is an array of entry objects, applied in order. For each, the existing entry with that id (if any) is patched and re-inserted, otherwise a new entry is created from defaults, and the entry is saved to settings. Earlier entries stay applied if a later one fails. An empty array succeeds without changes. A normal non-empty object is traversed as a list of its member values, so it fails 107 unless every member is an object. Absent params has no established safe response. The grade reflects the whole request/reply path, which reaches the shared diagnostic logger; it does not by itself mean the method changes device settings.

Side effects: Erases and re-inserts entries in the shared sequence map and persists each one to the sequence settings; checks free storage against an estimate. Every call also performs shared request/reply diagnostic logging.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_sequence"`. [READ] |
| `params` | array<object> | yes | - | Array of entry objects (required). See the entry schema. [READ] |
| `params[].id` | integer | yes | - | Entry id: JSON integer, not -1. Missing, wrong type or -1 gives 200. [READ] |
| `params[].type` | string | no | light | Frame type name. Recognised names (the table, exact-match; case handling not established): light, dark, bias, flat. Any other string maps to unknown. Read without a type check. [READ] |
| `params[].filter` | integer | no | 0 | Filter wheel slot index. Read without a type check; units and valid range not established. [READ] |
| `params[].suffix` | string | no | - | File name suffix. Read without a type check (a non-string reaches a length call). [READ] |
| `params[].exp` | number | no | 0 | Exposure; integer or float accepted. Unit not established by the parser. [READ] |
| `params[].gain` | integer | no | -1 | Camera gain; scale not established. [READ] |
| `params[].bin` | integer | no | 0 | Binning factor (INFERRED). [INFERRED] |
| `params[].repeat` | integer | no | 0 | Number of frames to capture (INFERRED). [INFERRED] |
| `params[].capture_index` | integer | no | 0 | Capture-control selector (INFERRED); meaning not established. [INFERRED] |
| `params[].enable` | boolean | no | True | Whether the entry is active. Disabled entries bypass the free-space check. [READ] |
| `params[].autoexp` | boolean | no | False | Auto exposure flag. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | An entry (or, for non-array params, a member) is not an object | `expected object param` |
| 200 | An entry id is missing, not an integer, or -1 | `invalid id` |
| 224 | Exposure mode 2 is active and either the capture thread is running or the total lapsed count of enabled entries is neither zero nor equal to their total repeat count | `cannot edit sequence unless reset the progress` |
| 208 | Estimated size of enabled sequences plus 150 MB exceeds free space (a decreased remaining count and disabled entries bypass the check) | `disk is full` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Helper errors outside the audited branches are unresolved.

## Example

Request, two-entries - Two light-frame entries (values invented):

```json
{"id":61,"method":"set_sequence","params":[{"id":1,"type":"light","filter":0,"suffix":"L","exp":10,"gain":80,"bin":1,"repeat":30,"capture_index":0,"enable":true,"autoexp":false},{"id":2,"type":"dark","exp":10,"repeat":20}]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_sequence","result":0,"code":0,"id":61}
```

Reply, locked:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_sequence","error":"cannot edit sequence unless reset the progress","code":224,"id":62}
```
